{{Short description|Russian physicist}}
'''Serguei Vladilenovich Krasnikov''' ({{langx|ru|Серге́й Владиле́нович Кра́сников}}; 10 September 1961 – 19 March 2024) was a Russian [[physicist]], [[Doctor of Sciences]] in Physical and Mathematical Sciences, graduate of [[Leningrad State University]]. He became famous for his contributions to [[theoretical physics]], in particular the development and mathematical modeling of the [[Krasnikov tube]] and its influence on the principle of causality, [[closed timelike curve]]s and [[superluminal motion]].

==Life==
Krasnikov obtained a doctorate ([[kandidat nauk|CSc.]]) in physics and mathematics from Leningrad State University in 1985. In 1987–1990 he worked at the Navy Institute of Radioelectronics. From 1990 to his death in 2024 he was based at [[Pulkovo Observatory]] in St. Petersburg, Russia.

Krasnikov's work was focused on theoretical physics, specifically on the development of the [[Krasnikov tube]] and its applications in causality, [[closed timelike curves]], and hyperfast travel.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Krasnikov|first=S. V.|date=1998-04-15|title=Hyperfast Interstellar Travel in General Relativity|journal=Physical Review D|volume=57|issue=8|pages=4760–4766|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.57.4760|issn=0556-2821|arxiv=gr-qc/9511068|bibcode=1998PhRvD..57.4760K|s2cid=55825213}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Krasnikov|first=S.|date=October 2008|title=Falling into the Schwarzschild black hole. Important details|journal=Gravitation and Cosmology|volume=14|issue=4|pages=362–367|doi=10.1134/S0202289308040129|issn=0202-2893|arxiv=0804.3619|bibcode=2008GrCo...14..362K|s2cid=17916871}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv|last=Krasnikov|first=S. V.|date=2000-03-22|title=Toward a Traversable Wormhole|eprint=gr-qc/0003092 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Krasnikov|first=S.|date=September 2000|title=A traversable wormhole|journal=Physical Review D|volume=62|issue=8|article-number=084028|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.62.084028|issn=0556-2821|arxiv=gr-qc/9909016|bibcode=2000PhRvD..62h4028K|s2cid=118517964}}</ref>

In 2001, Krasnikov worked at [[Starlab]], in a joint NASA/USAF-funded project to assess the viability of time travel under realistic physical conditions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Krasnikov|first=S.|date=2014-07-24|title=Time machines with the compactly determined Cauchy horizon|journal=Physical Review D|volume=90|issue=2|article-number=024067|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.90.024067|issn=1550-7998|arxiv=1405.2277|bibcode=2014PhRvD..90b4067K|s2cid=119312799}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv|last=Krasnikov|first=S.|date=2003-05-19|title=Time machine (1988--2001)|eprint=gr-qc/0305070 }}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv|last=Krasnikov|first=S.|date=2003-02-26|title=The wormhole hazard|eprint=r-qc/0302107 }}</ref>

In 2002, he attended the 11th UK Conference on the Foundations of Physics hosted by the [[Faculty of Philosophy, University of Oxford]] at which he delivered the paper "Time machine (1988–2001)".<ref name="11th at Oxford">{{cite web |last1=Morgan |first1=Peter |title=11th UK Conference on the Foundations of Physics |url=https://inspirehep.net/conferences/974538 |website=inspirehep.net |publisher=Inspire |access-date=19 June 2022}}</ref>
